explain.say: Ducks float well because they are light for their size. Air trapped in their feathers and in air sacs inside the body makes them much less dense than water, so only a little of the duck needs to sink to hold it up.

explain.say: Feathers keep the duck dry. They interlock so tightly that water beads off, and the duck keeps them in shape by preening with oil from a gland near its tail, so a layer of air stays against its body.

parts.ask: How do a duck's webbed feet work?

explain.say: To swim, a duck kicks each foot backwards with the webs spread wide, like a paddle. On the return stroke it folds its toes together so the foot slips forward through the water with little drag.

faq.q: Why do ducks float so well?
faq.a: Ducks are light for their size because air is trapped in their feathers and in air sacs inside their body. Being much less dense than water, a duck only needs to sink a little way for the water's upthrust to hold up its weight.
asks: How does a duck stay on top of the water?

faq.q: How do a duck's webbed feet work?
faq.a: On the power stroke the duck pushes its foot back with the toes spread, so the web acts like a wide paddle. On the way forward it folds the toes together, so the foot meets little water.
asks: Why do ducks have webbed feet?

faq.a: A duck's feathers are made of tiny branches that hook together so tightly that water cannot get through, and preening with oil keeps them neat. Air stays trapped next to the skin, so the duck stays warm and dry.

faq.q: Why don't ducks' feet freeze in icy water?
faq.a: The arteries and veins in a duck's legs run side by side. Warm blood going down heats the cold blood coming back, so the feet stay cold but just above freezing and lose very little body heat.
asks: How do ducks stand on ice?

faq.q: How do diving ducks go underwater?
faq.a: Diving ducks press air out of their feathers and air sacs to float lower, and their legs are set far back for powerful kicks. Dabbling ducks like mallards just tip up, tail in the air, to feed.
asks: Why do ducks tip upside down?

facts: Ducks preen with oil from the uropygial gland at the base of the tail.
Warm and cold blood swap heat in a duck's legs, so its feet lose little heat in icy water.
